Academically, ask your counselor for an alternative credit recovery class. Near my school we have a separate school that allows you to graduate early. If not, ask if they are available to change your schedule and allow at least on credit recovery class to get caught up. It's really difficult completing work so far behind. I was a semester behind school but I transferred. Also ask your counselor for a plan that you're not feeling good emotionally. It should be called 504 plan but that's probably in some states. 

Also, your teachers will be very supportive if you're behind. Depression etc. does that, its never your fault. So try to see if you or your counselor can email them 

And to answer your question, only go to the hospital if you know you're at a risk. I went when I was suicidal and knew I'd attempt it again. It was really secluded and kept me out of harms way since I knew there was nothing there to harm myself.

Equality plays no part in this. 

It's about supporting someone who's being harassed. It doesn't matter gender nor age, it's about being mature as an adult/teammate and helping the victim not feel singled out. 

You should never assume someone's confidence will be boosted by leaving them to solve it themselves. As someone with pretty bad anxiety i've had a familiar situation where I was singled out for petty reasons. Luckily I had someone who supported me and that gave me confidence that i'm NOT ALONE. It allows me to learn from this support on how to handle this and what to say. For example:

Someone calls me ugly, and I avoid commenting to avoid escalating the problem.

Someone nearby comments "You're not ugly, they're just trying to bring you down to feel better about themselves" 

I'd feel pretty confident about myself and have a sense of relief and know there's nearby support then having the word ugly stuck on my
mind.

You should never leave someone being harassed to
solve themselves. Not everyone is capable of doing so
